It's the Tetris Effect/Game Transfer Phenomena, our brains are weird, basically when you spend hours intensely focused on a game, your brain temporarily prioritizes that game's logic as its default way of scanning the environment, so when you leave the game it's still doing that, and it naturally goes away after a little while. It's your brain basically helping you focus better on the task you needed to do. You're not going to suddenly rob a bank because you played GTA for a long time.

This type of stuff isn't really limited to videogames, if you're doing a lot of office work and for example doing "ctrl + z", and then you spill your coffee, or you're writing by hand and mess up, maybe you'll mentally do "ctrl + z" to fix it. It's completely harmless and not permanent, this isn't an argument for people becoming more violent by playing videogames, but it might be a sign you should take a break.
